verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — X. Three verified, material differences all favour X. (1) Y carries a fabricated citation on the load-bearing (c) answer: it cites bin/cc-do:69-71 as a header remark naming launchd/com.claude.deploy-live as the unattended runner, but those lines are the activation-marker library resolution comment and mention neither. (2) Y asserts as a grep result that 'bin/cc-premise contains no literal reference to \"deploy-live\" anywhere in its own source' — false, it appears at :1528 and :2544. (3) Y fails brief part (b) materially: it dismisses scripts/deploy-parity-assert.sh en masse as plain comments when that file has 9 non-comment occurrences, one of which (:1459) the key names by name as required; Y also never adjudicates bin/cc-do:454 (key M2) while X both counts it and proves it reachable. Y additionally claims, 'confirmed (760-800)', that deploy-live.sh:708-746 only reach a .page file and are 'never executed' — refuted four lines past where Y stopped reading, at :812. X's only comparable defect is an off-by-one (cc-do:358 for the :359 invocation) plus a wrong grep denominator (273 vs 316), which is a precision error against Y's cluster of wrong facts.

X vs Z — X, narrowly. Z is the better-cited output by a clear margin: I opened 38 of its citations and found zero bad ones, against X's misreport of the key's S5 anchor line (bin/cc-do:358/:357 for the :359 invocation and :358 CONFIRM arm) and X's wrong in-scope grep count (273 vs the true 316, which Z gives exactly). Z is also more complete on (b) and contributes several verified facts X lacks (the --falsify-host mode exits at :339-408 before the arg loop at :411; the cc-backlog:3046 → :3579 claim chain; fix() at deploy-link-parity.sh:159; cc-blockers:642 rendered only at :1299/:1582/:1596). X wins anyway on the brief's central question — whether every execution site was found. Z rejects bin/cc-do:454 with a universal negative, 'None of the non-comment deploy-live lines in scope passes it as a --run argument', which is false and is refuted by a row in Z's own near-miss table: I verified scripts/deploy-live.sh:812 files `--run \"$run\"` with $run built at :708/:728/:731/:734/:743/:746, cc-backlog:1890/:2254/:2282 stores it as the JSON `run` field, cc-do:415 reads `.run`, and cc-do:454 executes it. X is the only output that establishes that chain, and it is a stronger emitter than the key's own M2 example (cc-blockers:642, whose recover_cmd Z itself proved is display-only). A wrong conclusion about whether a genuine execution path exists outranks a ±1 line number on a site both identified, quoted and explained correctly — hence X, but narrowly.

Y vs Z — Z, decisively. Z has no bad citations in 38 checked; Y has a fabricated one (cc-do:69-71), a false asserted grep (cc-premise has no 'deploy-live' literal — it has two), a quoted-string-not-in-range citation (deploy-now.sh:68-72 for text at :73/:77), an off-by-one on the S5r emit (:185-186 for :186-187), and a comment cited as evidence for the ▶ gate with the wrong line ('359-ish' for :386). On brief part (b) Z is the most complete list produced by any of the three while Y falsely excludes a whole file (deploy-parity-assert.sh) and omits validate-bash:1425, permission-gate-lint :526/:535/:637/:770/:782, test-hermeticity-lint, offbox-admission-lint:274, cc-venue:187 and cc-do:194. Both share the N4 miss and both mishandle cc-do:454, but Z at least adjudicates it explicitly (key M2) whereas Y is silent, and Z verified deploy-link-parity's fix() body that Y expressly could not.
